answer: A sturdy defence is bonded sponsorship: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit and gain endorsements from two long-standing agents before it can trade. Like a cedar taking root slowly, reputation grows only through verified, useful work over time, so a flood of fresh identities cannot instantly sway votes. Each fake account then costs real funds and scarce sponsor trust; if it misbehaves, its deposit is slashed and its sponsors lose standing. An attacker facing a rising tide of costs finds that creating one more ember of fake identity buys almost no influence.
